proposals.before: When the Ming destroyed the Liang princely house and extinguished Dali, they ruled through native chiefs, organizing the region into Pacification Commissioners, Pacification Supervisors, Reassurance Commissioners, principal and deputy native chiefs, native prefectures, and native subprefectures.
proposals.after: When the Ming defeated the Prince of Liang and extinguished Dali, they ruled through native chiefs, organizing the region into Pacification Commissioners, Pacification Supervisors, Reassurance Commissioners, principal and deputy native chiefs, native prefectures, and native subprefectures.
proposals.reason: Chinese 破梁王 refers to defeating the Prince of Liang as a titled person; rendering it as an impersonal princely house obscures the personal referent present in the Chinese and literal.

proposals.before: In the twenty-first year, they were taken; Shifan killed himself, and Yunnan was fully settled.
proposals.after: In the twenty-first year, they were overcome; Shifan killed himself, and Yunnan was fully settled.
proposals.reason: 克之 means the rebels were crushed or overcome, not that unspecified persons were captured; the idiomatic rendering already has the intended military sense.

proposals.before: Lu Wanzhong, however, was dominated by a Han collaborator, who persuaded him to send three thousand men from Zhenxiong against Dingkun at Ludian; Ortai dispatched Mobile Corps Commander Ha Yuansheng, who routed them;
proposals.after: Lu Wanzhong, however, was controlled by a Han collaborator; he arranged for three thousand troops from Zhenxiong to attack Dingkun at Ludian; Ortai dispatched Mobile Corps Commander Ha Yuansheng, who routed them;
proposals.reason: Chinese 約 marks Lu Wanzhong as arranging the attack; the idiomatic relative clause invents a persuasion sequence in which the collaborator is the grammatical agent of the troop levy.

proposals.before: Ortai assembled more than ten thousand regular troops, with native auxiliaries numbering half as many again, and advanced in three columns.
proposals.after: Ortai assembled more than ten thousand regular troops, with native auxiliaries numbering half as many, and advanced in three columns.
proposals.reason: Chinese 土兵半之 means native troops equal to half the regular force, not 'half as many again' (150%).

proposals.before: In the sixth year Ortai became governor-general of all three provinces. The native subprefecture of Anyufan, the Zhenyuan native prefecture under Diao Huan, the Zhele chief, and the various native chiefs of Weiyuan and Guangnan were impeached and removed one after another.
proposals.after: In the sixth year Ortai became governor-general of all three provinces. An Yufan of the native subprefecture, Diao Huan of the Zhenyuan native prefecture, the Zhele chief, and the various native chiefs of Weiyuan and Guangnan were impeached and removed one after another.
proposals.reason: Parallel 土州安於蕃 with 鎮沅土府刁澣 shows 安於蕃 is a personal name, not a place-name Anyufan.

proposals.before: In the sixth year Ortai governed all three provinces; the native subprefecture of Anyufan, the native prefecture of Zhenyuan under Diao Huan, the chief official of Zhele, and the various native chiefs of Weiyuan Subprefecture and Guangnan Prefecture were impeached and removed in succession.
proposals.after: In the sixth year Ortai governed all three provinces; An Yufan of the native subprefecture, Diao Huan of the Zhenyuan native prefecture, the chief official of Zhele, and the various native chiefs of Weiyuan Subprefecture and Guangnan Prefecture were impeached and removed in succession.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 安於蕃 as a place; it is the native-subprefecture holder An Yufan.

proposals.before: The line passed to Yang Rongchang; in the fiftieth year of Qianlong (1785) the office was reclassified as a hereditary ninth-rank native post.
proposals.after: The line passed to Yang Rongchang; in the fiftieth year of Qianlong (1785) the office was reclassified as a hereditary secondary ninth-rank native post.
proposals.reason: 從九品 is the secondary (从) ninth rank, not the full ninth rank; the idiomatic rendering drops 從.

proposals.before: His great-grandson A Kouyuan had indulged bandits and harmed the people; in the fourth year of Yongzheng (1726) the post was abolished, he was resettled in Jiangxi, and the territory was brought under regular administration.
proposals.after: His great-grandson A Kouyuan had indulged bandits and harmed the people; in the fourth year of Yongzheng (1726) the post was converted to regular administration and he was resettled in Jiangxi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 改流，安插江西 is conversion to regular administration plus resettlement; the idiomatic version invents a separate abolition clause not present as 裁/除.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), he joined Wang Lu's rebellion and was put to death. His lands were organized as Kaifua Prefecture under regular magistrates.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), he joined Wang Lu's rebellion and was put to death. His lands were organized as Kaihua Prefecture under regular magistrates.
proposals.reason: 開化府 is standardly romanized Kaihua, not Kaifua.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Kangxi, he followed Wang Lu in rebellion and was executed; his territory became Kaifua Prefecture and regular officials were appointed.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Kangxi, he followed Wang Lu in rebellion and was executed; his territory became Kaihua Prefecture and regular officials were appointed.
proposals.reason: 開化府 is standardly romanized Kaihua, not Kaifua.

proposals.before: The Deputy Chief Official of the Chief Official of Wangnong Mountain.
proposals.after: The Deputy Chief Official of Wangnong Mountain.
proposals.reason: Literal English redundantly stacks offices; Chinese names the deputy chief of Wangnong Mountain.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), Shuo joined Lu Changxian's rebellion. Government forces marched against him; Shuo burned himself alive, and his territory was annexed to Kaifua Prefecture.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), Shuo joined Lu Changxian's rebellion. Government forces marched against him; Shuo burned himself alive, and his territory was annexed to Kaihua Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 開化府 should be Kaihua, not Kaifua.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Kangxi, Shuo rebelled with Lu Changxian; government troops attacked; Shuo burned himself to death; his territory was placed under Kaifua Prefecture.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Kangxi, Shuo rebelled with Lu Changxian; government troops attacked; Shuo burned himself to death; his territory was placed under Kaihua Prefecture.
proposals.reason: 開化府 should be Kaihua, not Kaifua.

proposals.before: In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), Rishen's sons Shifan and Shiping joined Ning's Lu Changxian in rebellion. Regional Commander Yan Zhen crushed the uprising.
proposals.after: In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), Rifang's younger brother Rishen's sons Shifan and Shiping joined Ning's Lu Changxian in rebellion. Regional Commander Yan Zhen crushed the uprising.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits 日芳弟 identifying Rishen as Rifang's younger brother.

proposals.before: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi of the Qing, when Yunnan was recovered, the native Wang Feng was given a false post as Mobile Corps Commander, was met on the Guangxi road, and submitted in allegiance.
proposals.after: In the nineteenth year of Kangxi of the Qing, when Yunnan was recovered, the native Wang Feng was given a false post as Mobile Corps Commander; he went to the Guangxi road and submitted in allegiance.
proposals.reason: Chinese 迎至廣西路投誠 has Wang Feng proceeding to the Guangxi road to submit; English "was met" reverses the agency of 迎至.

proposals.before: A later holder was dismissed for misconduct; the line passed to Shen Zhaoqian.
proposals.after: Later he was dismissed for a crime; the line passed to Shen Zhaoqian.
proposals.reason: Chinese 後以罪黜 has a silent subject continued from the hereditary office narrative; "A later holder" invents an unnamed distinct holder not stated in the source.

decisions.reason: 明破梁王 names the titled Prince of Liang as the defeated party; 'destroyed the Liang princely house' impersonalizes 梁王 and diverges from the personal referent already clear in s0004.
克之 is the military taking/overcoming of the rebel position, not capture of unspecified persons; 'they were taken' misreads the verb, while 'overcome' matches the sense already in the idiomatic field.
After 制于漢奸, 約鎮雄兵三千攻鼎坤 keeps Lu Wanzhong as the arranger of the levy; the relative clause invents a persuasion sequence and makes the collaborator the agent of sending the troops.

decisions.reason: 土兵半之 means native troops equal to half the regular force; 'half as many again' wrongly yields 150% of the regulars.
Parallel 土州安於蕃 with 鎮沅土府刁澣 marks 安於蕃 as the personal name of the native-subprefecture holder, not a place-name Anyufan.

decisions.reason: Same parallel: 安於蕃 is the person holding the native subprefecture, paired with Diao Huan of Zhenyuan, not a place called Anyufan.

decisions.reason: 從九品 is the secondary (从) ninth rank; omitting 從 as plain 'ninth-rank' upgrades the office beyond the Chinese grade.
Chinese has only 改流，安插江西—conversion to regular administration plus resettlement; the idiomatic triads a separate 'abolished' clause not present as 裁/除.
開化府 romanizes as Kaihua; Kaifua misreads 化 as fua.
Same romanization error in the literal field: 開化府 is Kaihua, not Kaifua.
王弄山長官司副長官 names the deputy chief of the Wangnong Mountain chief-official office; stacking 'Deputy Chief Official of the Chief Official' is redundant mistranslation.
Again 開化府 must be Kaihua; Kaifua is an erroneous romanization.
Literal field repeats the Kaifua error; 開化府 is Kaihua.

decisions.after: In the fourth year of Kangxi (1665), the sons of Rifang's younger brother Rishen, Shifan and Shiping, joined Ning's Lu Changxian in rebellion. Regional Commander Yan Zhen crushed the uprising.
decisions.reason: Idiomatic English omits 日芳弟, a real kinship error; the proposed string restores that fact but is garden-path awkward, so rephrase as 'the sons of Rifang's younger brother Rishen, Shifan and Shiping'.

decisions.reason: 迎至廣西路投誠 has Wang Feng going to the Guangxi road to submit; 'was met' reverses the agency of 迎至.
後以罪黜 continues the silent hereditary-office subject and does not introduce a new unnamed holder; 'A later holder' invents a person the Chinese does not name.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0008 shows s0101 states 改流 rather than a separate abolition; the office claim's action must track conversion to regular administration, not the invented 'abolished' wording.
